heroLede: Shape your sound on Windows 10/11 with equalization, effects, and audio analysis in one focused workspace.
featuresIntro: From basic tone shaping to context-based listening tools. Choose an effect and adjust it step by step.
fEqText: Adjust 31 Hz to 16 kHz and view the response curve as you make changes.
fToneText: Add weight to the low end or brightness to the high frequencies.
fDialogueText: Shape the midrange to bring voices forward to your preference.
fVirtualText: Adjust perceived width or add a gentle crossfeed for headphones.
fReverbText: Load a WAV impulse response for convolution; results depend on the file and device.
fLimiterText: Taylor Engine limits peaks to help reduce clipping when gain is increased.
fPresetText: Start with music, movie, game, voice, or headphone presets and make them yours.
fAutoText: The desktop app can use rules to select a preset based on the active application.
featureNote: Some modes require Equalizer APO or VB-CABLE; compatibility depends on Windows settings and audio drivers.
demoIntro: The demo creates tones and pink noise with Web Audio on your device. Start at a low volume.
demoLimit: This is a browser simulation. The desktop app uses its selected audio engine to process Windows audio routes.
demoUnsupported: This browser does not support Web Audio.

howIntro: Each mode has its own requirements and limits. Review the signal path before choosing.
modeAText: Writes configuration for Equalizer APO on an endpoint selected in its Configurator.

modeAReq2: Exclusive, ASIO, or bitstream audio may bypass processing.

modeBReq2: Latency, endpoint, and driver affect the result.

compatNote: No single route supports every driver. Try your own devices and use the recovery tools if needed.
downloadIntro: Taylor ND Audio targets 64-bit Windows 10/11. Releases will be posted on the project page.
downloadWait: There is no release download link yet.
requirementNotice: The virtual cable is not bundled with the installer.
faqIntro: Learn about compatibility, installation permissions, and audio handling.
faq1Q: Which apps may not be processed?
faq1A: WASAPI exclusive, ASIO, or bitstream audio may bypass supported processing routes. Results also vary with endpoint, driver, spatial audio, and Windows mode.
faq2Q: How should I test before regular use?
faq2A: Start at a low volume, check several apps and endpoints, and if possible try it in a virtual machine or on a non-critical device first.
faq3A: Use Restore Audio in the app to disable processing. For Taylor Engine, stop the engine and restore the playback device in Windows. Restart Windows if the endpoint does not recover immediately.
faq4Q: Why do some steps need Administrator access?
faq4A: Installing Equalizer APO, VB-CABLE, or registering system-level effects may require administrator permission. Only elevate installers or actions you intentionally start.
faq5Q: Is audio or other information sent online?
faq5A: The website does not request a microphone or audio device for its demo, and sample audio is not uploaded. The desktop app processes audio locally; a compatibility report is only written when you export it.
faq6Q: Is Taylor ND Audio certified for every driver?
faq6A: No. Processing depends on endpoint, driver, Windows configuration, and playback mode. The app reports what it detects, known limits, and fallback options.
